slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
In a 30-60-90 triangle, the hypotenuse is twice the short leg, and the long leg is √3 times the short leg: sides x, x√3, 2x.

Fold an equilateral triangle of side 2x along an altitude. The altitude bisects the base, so the short leg is x, opposite the 30 degree angle. By the Pythagorean Theorem the altitude is √((2x)2 − x2) = √(3x2) = x√3, opposite the 60 degree angle.
